subject: DELETE statement
notes: || UPHELD with independent evidence. GR4 --check OK. Code READ myself, both halves. Staging: KeyedIoEmitter.EmitDelete opens with 'if (file.Organization == FileOrganization.Relative && file.AccessMode != FileAccessMode.Sequential) { if (Rrn(file) is not { } rrn) { w.Line(LoudStmt(...)); return; } w.Line($"{RuntimeApi.FileSetRelativeKey(name, rrn)};"); }' -- so RANDOM and DYNAMIC both stage the RELATIVE KEY item's current value, and an unresolvable RELATIVE KEY is LOUD, never a silent no-op. RelativeConnector.SetPendingKey is 'public void SetPendingKey(long rrn) => _pendingKey = rrn;' and touches nothing else (this also matters for GR9). Removal: RelativeConnector.Delete's non-sequential arm is 'if (!_slots.Remove(_pendingKey)) return Status = FileStatusCode.RecordNotFound; return Status = FileStatusCode.Success;' -- removal by staged key, '23' when absent, which is the 9.1.14 invalid key condition routed by the same EmitInvalid/EmitUseHook pair as GR3. An RRN of 0 or negative also lands on '23', which is right: unlike WRITE (14.9.51 GR29b -> '34') GR4 states only the not-contained case. Test re-read and confirmed spec-derived: tests/conformance/2002/file_sharing_mutate.cob declares 'SELECT F-Q ... ORGANIZATION IS RELATIVE, ACCESS MODE IS RANDOM, RELATIVE KEY IS Q-KEY' and executes 'DELETE F-Q RECORD.' with Q-KEY = 1; the golden shows DELQ=00 then READQ23=23 on that same key through that same connector, so the slot named by the key really was the one removed. || NOT covered by any test (read only): the invalid-key half reaching an INVALID KEY imperative on the DELETE path itself. That, not the removal half, is what remains to close.
